title: Streaming Tokens & Robust Error Handling in .NET
description: Stream tokens in real-time using IAsyncEnumerable, handle mid-stream disconnections, manage CancellationToken propagation, and recover from 429 rate limits.

data.text: The Engineering Reality of Token Streaming

Generating long LLM responses can take anywhere from 3 to 30 seconds. If an application waits for the entire completion to finish before returning any data, users perceive the system as frozen or unresponsive. Streaming tokens as they are emitted solves perceived latency (reducing Time To First Token to under 500ms). However, streaming introduces distributed systems complexity: client disconnects mid-stream, network drops, token rate-limit spikes halfway through a response, and partial completion states.

In .NET, streaming LLM completions utilize IAsyncEnumerable<StreamingChatCompletionUpdate>. You must always pass the HttpContext.RequestAborted CancellationToken so that if the user closes their browser or cancels the request, downstream inference is immediately aborted, preventing wasted cloud tokens.

data.text: Common Streaming Failure Modes and Mitigations

rows: Detect RequestAborted token cancellation; break loop immediately to conserve tokens
Token per minute (TPM) quota exhausted during a long output
Emit an SSE error event: 'event: error' informing React UI to present a retry button
LLM started generating text that violated content safety thresholds
Catch System.ClientModel.ClientResultException; emit a safety violation notice to the frontend
ASP.NET Core or reverse proxy (Nginx) buffering HTTP output
Set Response.Headers['X-Accel-Buffering'] = 'no' and call Response.Body.FlushAsync() after every token batch

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Streaming reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) from seconds to milliseconds, drastically improving UX
Use IAsyncEnumerable and CompleteChatStreamingAsync for zero-allocation streaming in C#
Always propagate HttpContext.RequestAborted to cancel cloud model inference when users disconnect
Flush the response body (FlushAsync) after emitting tokens to prevent proxy buffering stalls
Emit formal Server-Sent Events (SSE) events to signal completion ([DONE]) or mid-stream errors
data.takeaway: Reliable streaming requires proactive error handling and cancellation awareness. Linking CancellationToken from client to model ensures responsive UX without runaway compute costs.
